## Literature review (checked 2026-08-17)

**Status:** open  
**Classification:** OPEN-TRIAGE

**Current literature assessment.** The number of distinct pinned-distance counts is not known to be (1-o(1))n.

**Verified partial progress.**

- Erdős--Fishburn prove g(n)>3n/8.
- Csizmadia improves the lower bound to g(n)>7n/10.
- Known configurations give g(n)<n-cn^(2/3) for some constant c>0.

**Full solution or refutation.**

No later improvement or resolution was located; formalization of the statement does not alter its status.

Raise the lower constant toward 1 or improve the upper obstruction sufficiently to refute the conjectured ratio.

statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j
eq i\}$, where the points are ordered such that $ R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n). $ Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of distinct values the $R(x_i)$ can take. Is it true that $g(n) \geq (1-o(1))n$?
title: Erdős Problem #653
